wikitext.*: {{short description|American college basketball season}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=August 2023}} {{Infobox college sports team season |year=2020–21 |team=Grand Canyon Antelopes |sport=Basketball |image=Grand Canyon Antelopes logo.svg |image_size=250 |conference=Western Athletic Conference |division= |short_conf= WAC |APRank= |CoachRank= |record= 17–7 |conf_record= 9–3 |head_coach=[[Bryce Drew]] |hc_year = 1st |asst_coach1=[[Jamall Walker]] |asst_coach2=[[Ed Schilling]] |asst_coach3=[[Casey Shaw]] |stadium=[[GCU Arena]] |champion= WAC regular season co–champions and tournament champions |tourney=[[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], first round |tourney_result= }} {{2020–21 WAC men's basketball standings}} The '''2020–21 Grand Canyon Antelopes men's basketball team''' represented [[Grand Canyon University]] during the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. They were led by first-year head coach [[Bryce Drew]] and played their home games at [[GCU Arena]] in [[Phoenix, Arizona]] as members of the [[Western Athletic Conference]] (WAC). They finished the season 17–7, 9–3 in WAC play, to finish in a tie for the regular-season championship. They defeated [[2020–21 Seattle Redhawks men's basketball team|Seattle]]{{Cite web |last=Coro |first=Paul |date=2021-03-12 |title=GCU rolls to WAC championship game |url=https://gculopes.com/news/2021/3/12/rapid-recap-gcu-rolls-to-championship-game.aspx |access-date=2024-10-08 |website=Grand Canyon University Athletics |language=en}} and [[2020–21 New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball team|New Mexico State]]{{Cite web |last=Coro |first=Paul |date=2021-03-13 |title=Let's dance: GCU heads to NCAA tourney |url=https://gculopes.com/news/2021/3/14/mens-basketball-lets-dance-gcu-heads-to-ncaa-tourney.aspx |access-date=2024-10-08 |website=Grand Canyon University Athletics |language=en}} to win the [[2021 WAC men's basketball tournament|WAC tournament]] and received the conference's automatic bid to the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where they lost in the first round to [[2020–21 Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball team|Iowa]].{{Cite web |last=Coro |first=Paul |date=2021-03-20 |title=Lopes make 1st impression in tourney loss |url=https://gculopes.com/news/2021/3/20/mens-basketball-lopes-make-1st-impression-in-tourney-loss.aspx |access-date=2024-10-08 |website=Grand Canyon University Athletics |language=en}} == Previous season == The [[2019–20 Grand Canyon Antelopes men's basketball team|Antelopes]] finished the [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20 season]] 13–17, 8–8 in WAC play, to finish in a tie for fifth place. They were set to be the No. 4 seed in the [[2020 WAC men's basketball tournament|WAC tournament]]; however, the tournament was canceled amid concerns over the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]].{{Cite web |last=Martinez |first=Justin |date=March 12, 2020 |title=WAC tournament cancelled due to coronavirus concerns |url=https://www.lcsun-news.com/story/sports/college/nmsu/2020/03/12/wac-tournament-cancelled-due-coronavirus-concerns/5029177002/ |access-date=2020-03-25 |website=Las Cruces Sun-News |language=en}} On March 13, 2020, the school fired [[Dan Majerle]] as head coach of the Antelopes.{{Cite web |last=Kasabian |first=Paul |date=March 13, 2020 |title=Dan Majerle Fired as Grand Canyon University HC After 7 Seasons |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2880689-dan-majerle-fired-as-grand-canyon-university-hc-after-7-seasons |access-date=2020-03-25 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}} A few days later, the school named former [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]] and [[Valparaiso Beacons men's basketball|Valparaiso]] head coach [[Bryce Drew]] as the Antelopes' next head coach.{{Cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=2020-03-17 |title=Bryce Drew hired as head coach at Grand Canyon |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28915889
